summary: Wire the Quality Gates workflow at .github/workflows so GitHub Actions can run it and required status checks can attach. The gate definition previously existed only as the distributable template at ci/.github/workflows/gates.yml, which GitHub never reads. A Greptile review of the wiring then found a shell injection and three correctness defects in that gate definition; those are fixed here in both copies, because wiring the workflow is what made them live.

unverified: BLOCKER: G-1 fails on this diff. ci/.github/workflows/gates.yml matches no pattern in ownership.yaml, so editing the template is UNOWNED for every bot. Fixing the injection required editing it, because the alternative was leaving the vulnerability in the copy README tells other repositories to seed from while simultaneously breaking the sync check this PR adds. The manifest needs a rule for ci/.github/workflows/** and ownership.yaml belongs to bot-06-quality-security, so this cannot be resolved from this seat.

No GitHub Actions run has been observed for either workflow. GitHub is not assigning runners to this repository: every job so far failed in 2-4 seconds with runner_id 0, no steps executed and logs returning HTTP 404, reproduced on a re-run. Everything recorded here is a local run.
The shell injection was reproduced and the fix verified locally by simulating GitHub's ${{ }} substitution. It has not been confirmed on a real runner, because no runner has started.
The diff-based receipt and contract-document selection has not run under a real pull_request event; the base ref and fetch depth behave differently under actions/checkout than in this working tree.
Unpinned action tags and unconstrained pip installs (Greptile P2) are not addressed. Pinning is a deliberate hardening pass across the gate tooling, not part of wiring the workflow.
Branch protection has not been configured — making these checks required status checks is a repository-settings action outside this diff.
bot-06-quality-security has not reviewed this change; the pull request is a draft.
rollback_plan: Revert the merge commit: `git revert -m 1 <sha>`. Recovery time is one push, under two minutes, and takes effect on the next workflow dispatch. Data implications: none — the workflows write no state. Reverting restores ci/.github/workflows/gates.yml to its previous content, which reinstates the shell injection in the distributable template, so a revert should be paired with either re-applying the env: changes to the template alone or removing the root workflow so nothing executes. Removing just .github/workflows/gates.yml and .github/workflows/gates-template-sync.yml is the safer partial rollback: it stops the gates running while leaving the hardened template in place.

approvals.blast_radius: Adds two workflows at the repository root and hardens the gate definition in both copies. Once branch protection marks them required, every pull request to main must pass G-1 through G-6 and the template-sync check. The receipt and contract-document selection changes make G-2 and G-4 stricter: a change that adds no receipt for its own bot now fails where it previously reused an older one.
